bindings.label: Patient had fever and left shoulder pain, and was found to have pericardial effusion
14-year-old male, weighing 45 kg, was transferred to our clinic after pericardial effusion was found at a provincial hospital
Initial symptoms included fever and left shoulder pain
Physical examination revealed reduced cardiac sound intensity and elevated heart rate
The patient did not exhibit arthralgia or abdominal pain at any point during the clinical course
Three weeks before this event, the patient had an upper respiratory tract infection treated with ibuprofen
Infectious pericarditis
Systemic inflammatory disease
Neoplastic/TB effusion
Ibuprofen-associated effusion
Laboratory tests show leukocytosis
CRP level is 131 and ESR is 72
ECG shows PR depression and ST elevation
Tests for tuberculosis, viral infection, and antinuclear antibodies are negative
NLRP12 mutation is detected and IL-1β level is 10 pg/mL
Pericardial effusion is moderate in size
Bacterial pericarditis
Viral pericarditis
Mycoplasma pneumoniae pericarditis
Tuberculous pericarditis
Differential leukocyte count shows neutrophilia
Post-upper-respiratory-infection bacterial pericarditis
White blood cell count is 19,670/µL with neutrophilic predominance
Pericardial fluid culture, blood culture, and procalcitonin remain pending with no organism identified
